To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

• We propose to train a speaker embedding model for speaker recognition with prototypical network (PN) loss, a metric learning approach that has been successfully applied to few shot image classification.

(1) PNL outperforms state of the art models in both seen and unseen speaker identification and verification, (2) PNL can be used to learn embeddings for unseen speakers, (3) PNL is robust to noise and reverberation, (4) PNL can learn embeddings for speakers with only one utterance, (5) PNL can also be used to learn speaker embeddings from raw waveform data.

1) PNL outperforms triplet loss in speaker verification and identification, for both seen speakers and unseen speakers, 2) PNL is more robust than triplet loss against the number of training speakers and the number of training utterances per speaker, and 3) the performance gap between seen and unseen speakers can be reduced by increasing the number of seen speakers.
